newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rate jitters glue German overnight rate at 3.12 pc.
newsitem.headline: Rate jitters glue German overnight rate at 3.12 pc.

text.p: German overnight rates remained glued at higher levels on Thursday, signalling market nervousness about the direction of German interest rates, only one week after the U.S. Federal Reserve hiked short-term rates.

"At times of uncertainty about the direction of interest rates, short-term rates often go up," said a senior money market trader, adding " only after expectations normalise a bit again, will be see rates coming off again."
Call money rates traded between 3.125/3.150 percent today, virtually unchanged from Wednesday's levels, when the Bundesbank also drained funds from the market.

While economists generally said the Bundesbank has absolutely no reason to follow the Federal Reserve's action as German inflationary dangers still appear under control, money market dealers said the nervousness about a potential hike was still palpable.
"When the U.S. market coughs, our nose starts to run," said another dealer explaining nervousness automatically ebbs across borders, even when there is no fundamental reason for concern.
Last week the U.S. Fed ended a 20-month easing period by raising its short-term fed funds rate to 5.50 percent, firing a preemptive volley against potential inflationary pressures.

The Bundesbank meets today and as expected left its three main rates steady, with the discount rate remaining at 2.50 percent, the Lombard at 4.50 percent and the main money market rate, the repo, at three percent.

Dealers offered another reason for current money market movements however, saying that a blip in rates at month-end, taken into account in time-deposits, have made short-term funds ever more popular and thus dear.
"Pricing in Lombard borrowings at month-end has made people move away from time deposits hoping to get better conditions in overnight funds," said a dealer.

Others noted although there was sufficient liquidity, banks were still reeling from recent month-end rate gyrations and were therefore more cautious, preferring to fulfil their minimum reserves as early as possible in the month.
"There is enough money out there, but banks are sitting on it. Based on the reserve figures, we should be trading much lower, closer to 3.08 or 3.09 percent," a dealer said.
"I think people are just being extra careful at the moment," added another dealer.
In light of these circumstances, dealers said they saw little chance for rates to come off soon.
On Wednesday's banks holdings in non-interest bearing accounts at the central bank fell to 41.7 billion marks from 44.6 billion marks on Tuesday.
Banks held an average 43.2 billion marks in the first days of the months, also down from the average level of 44.6 billion marks, held through Tuesday.
Lombard borrowings were negligible on Wednesday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was set at 3.15400 percent on Thursday after 3.15467 percent on Wednesday.
